Brock Purdy missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury, while Sam Darnold appears on track to return for a pivotal NFC West matchup

    6:10 pm ET

        The NFL is in the midst of its most chaotic week of the season. Due to the Thanksgiving holiday, we've embarked on a six-day stretch that includes five days of games. While the Packers and Rams get things started on Wednesday night, we still have the Thanksgiving triple-header and the Black Friday game before we even start talking about the regular Sunday slate and, of course, Monday Night Football.When you sprinkle in some utter madness between Aaron Rodgers and his now-former team, the Pittsburgh Steelers, there will be plenty to talk about around the dinner table this holiday season. Of course, one of the topics of conversation will also be injuries. They're an omnipresent aspect of the NFL and are a factor as we step into Week 12. Below, we examine every injury report across the league, as well as highlight the game statuses for Thanksgiving. All games are Sunday unless noted.Chicago Bears at Detroit Lions (Thursday)Bears: DB Kyler Gordon (shoulder), DB Elijah Hicks (concussion), RB Roschon Johnson (ankle) OUT; DB Tyrique Stevenson Sr. (groin), LB D'Marco Jackson (elbow) QUESTIONABLE Lions: DL Skyler Gill-Howard (knee), CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder) OUT; S Chuck Clark (hamstring), EDGE DJ Wonnum (back) QUESTIONABLEWhile Wednesday's practice was conducted as a walk-through, Tyrique Stevenson Sr. did pop up on the injury report with a groin injury. He was limited for the session and officially listed as questionable. 
Gill Howard nor Rakestraw practiced this week, so it's not surprising to see them ruled out. On a more positive note, Chuck Clark returned to practice on Tuesday and remained a limited participant during Wednesday's session. Moreover, pass rusher DJ Wonnum was limited on Wednesday after missing the first two practices of the week with a back injury. Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys (Thursday)Eagles: OLB Arnold Ebiketie (oblique), CB Jonathan Jones (ankle) OUTCowboys: G Tyler Booker (ankle), TE Jake Ferguson (knee, ankle), DB P.J. Locke (concussion), WR Jonathan Mingo (ankle) OUT; CB Devin Moore (hip), DB Jalen Thompson (hamstring) QUESTIONABLEQuinyon Mitchell carries no game designation, so the Eagles star corner is slated to play. He was a full participant during Wednesday's practice after missing Monday's session and being limited on Tuesday due to a hamstring injury. Dak Prescott was listed on the injury report this week with a left hand injury, but the Cowboys quarterback was a full participant throughout and has no game designation. Meanwhile, Booker and Ferguson did not practice at all this week and will be sidelined for Week 12. 
Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills (Thursday)Chiefs: RB Kenneth Walker III (groin), OL Jaylon Moore (ankle), DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) OUT; TE Noah Gray (rib), DL Peter Woods (neck) QUESTIONABLEBills: CB Christian Benford (groin), Dalton Kincaid (thumb, ankle), DT T.J. Sanders (shoulder), G O'Cyrus Torrence (ankle), LB Dorian Williams (calf) QUESTIONABLEFor the third straight week, the Chiefs will be without Kenneth Walker III. The star back continues to deal with a groin injury and, after practicing on a limited basis on Tuesday, did not participate on Wednesday. Emmett Johnson will once again assume the role as Kansas City's lead back. After missing Monday's session, Bills corner Christian Benford logged back-to-back limited days of practice and is officially questionable to play. Meanwhile, Kincaid, Sanders, Torrence and Williams were limited throughout the week. Denver Broncos at Pittsburgh SteelersThe Broncos have already ruled out safety Taylor Rapp and defensive end Sai'vion Jones (hamstring) for this Black Friday matchup with Pittsburgh. Elsewhere, the roster is pretty healthy as running back Tyler Badie (thumb), wide receiver Pat Bryant (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), tight end Caleb Lohner (foot) and safety JL Skinner (shoulder) were all full participants on Wednesday. 
Linebacker Alex Highsmith (ankle) and receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) both did not practice on Wednesday due to injury. Meanwhile, defensive tackle Cameron Heyward was given a rest day. Safety DeShon Elliott (knee), linebacker Nick Herbig (hip, ribs), and linebacker Cole Holcomb (heel) were all limited. New Orleans Saints at Cincinnati BengalsTight end Juwan Johnson was the lone player missing from practice as he deals with a hamstring and wrist injury. Guard David Edwards (hamstring), offensive tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), center Erik McCoy (biceps), offensive tackle Asim Richards (knee) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) were limited.New York Giants at Indianapolis ColtsPass rusher Abdul Carter did not practice on Wednesday due to ankle and calf injuries. John Harbaugh said Carter is day-to-day, but should play this weekend. Defensive tackle Shelby Harris and corner Andru Phillips also missed practice due to illness. Tight end Isaiah Likely (groin) and linebacker Arvell Reese (back) were limited.
Tight end Will Mallory (hamstring), running back Seth McGowan (hamstring), tight end Andrew Ogletree (knee), defensive tackle Jerry Tillery (calf), offensive tackle Jalen Travis (knee), and corner Charvarius Ward (knee) all missed Wednesday's practice for the Colts. New York Jets at Miami DolphinsRookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle, groin) and defensive lineman Harrison Phillips (ankle) were held out of Wednesday's practice for the Jets. Receiver Isaiah Williams (ribs), offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee) and edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle, foot) were limited. Miami held out corner Julius Brents (neck, shoulder), punter Bradley Pinion (right groin) and receiver Jared Wayne (quad) from the opening practice of the week. Linebacker Ronnie Harrison (hamstring), offensive tackle Austin Jackson (elbow, knee), defensive end Rodney McGraw (shoulder), safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder, groin) and linebacker Jackson Woodard (hand) were all limited. 
Atlanta Falcons at Minnesota VikingsAtlanta was without six players to begin the week of practice: receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring), receiver Jahan Dotson (hamstring), safety DeMarcco Hellams (foot), guard Matthew Bergeron (hamstring), defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) and defensive end Za'Darius Smith (rest). Defensive end James Pearce (back) was limited. The Vikings held a walk-through practice, so the initial injury report is an estimate. That said, receiver Jordan Addison (thumb), offensive tackle Christian Darrisaw (shoulder), defensive lineman Jalen Redmond (ankle), corner Isaiah Rodgers (thigh), and safety Harrison Smith (thigh) were held out. Receiver Tai Felton (hip), quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring) and receiver Myles Price (knee, groin) were limited. Tennessee Titans at Jacksonville JaguarsSafety Terrell Burgess (knee), corner Cor'Dale Flott (neck) and offensive tackle Dan Moore Jr. (knee) were listed as non-participants at practice for the Titans. Defensive tackle John Franklin-Myers (back) was limited. 
Running back Bhayshul Tuten was the only Jaguars player held out of Wednesday's practice as he deals with an ankle/foot injury. Defensive tackle Matt Dickerson (neck), linebacker Dennis Gardeck (neck), offensive lineman Robert Hainsey (knee), offensive tackle Walker Little (knee, receiver Jakobi Meyers (ankle, offensive lineman Jonah Monheim (ankle), defensive end Danny Striggow (concussion), offensive lineman Cole Van Lanen (ankle) and offensive lineman Patrick Mekari (back) were all limited. Baltimore Ravens at Houston TexansAnalysis to come.New England Patriots at Los Angeles ChargersAnalysis to come.Washington Commanders at Arizona CardinalsWashington listed Stefon Diggs as a non-participant during Wednesday's practice due to personal reasons. The only other player to miss the session was corner Amik Robertson due to an ankle injury. Receiver Treylon Burks (foot) and defensive end Charles Omenihu (rib) were limited. Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ersAfter missing two games due to quad and rib injuries, Sam Darnold returned to practice on Wednesday, and coach Mike Macdonald said he is on track to start, provided practice goes well. 
Quarterback Brock Purdy did not practice for the 49ers on Wednesday due to an ankle injury. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday that Purdy suffered the injury in the second quarter of last week's win over the Vikings and was able to finish the game. On top of Purdy, receiver Mike Evans (Achilles), receiver Jordan Watkins (groin), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck) and safety Siran Neal (knee, foot) were held out of practice. Corners Deommodore Lenoir (foot) and Upton Stout (shoulder, neck) were limited, along with offensive linemen Carver Willis (illness) and Austen Pleasants (knee). Las Vegas Raiders at Cleveland BrownsThe Raiders have listed Brock Bowers as a limited participant during Wednesday's practice as the tight end continues to deal with an ankle injury. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) was also limited, while defensive tackles Adam Butler (concussion) and Tim Keenan (knee) did not practice. Cleveland was without four players to start the week of practice: guard Austin Barber (knee), defensive end Derek Barnett (hamstring), receiver Denzel Boston (quad), and defensive end Isaiah McGuire (calf). Tight end Harold Fannin (groin) was limited, as were center Elgton Jenkins (knee), running back Raheim Sanders (hip), tight end Blake Whiteheart (hip) and linebacker Quincy Williams (knee).

Here are the latest news and rumors from the MLB hot stove on Wednesday, Nov. 25
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:23 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Hello, Thanksgiving Eve. This is generally not a day for a bevy of MLB moves, but with the CBA expiration right around the corner, there's been a flurry of moves this week. Perhaps that carries over for one more day until we get to Turkey Day? Buckle up. Here are the latest news and rumors from around the league. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cubs looking to add two more starting pitchersThe Cubs have already signed lefty Trevor Rogers for rotation help, but they had such huge free agent losses that they'll need much more there. Sure enough, they are looking to add "at least two more guys that are no doubt rotation pieces," The Athletic reports. That could come via trade and/or free agency. The Cubs rotation right now is Rogers, Justin Steele (returning from Tommy John surgery), Edward Cabrera (terrible in 2026), Javier Assad and, I guess, Braxton Garrett. Ben Brown and Cade Horton are recovering from major surgery and top prospect Jaxon Wiggins battled injuries and an exploding ERA in Triple-A last season. The Cubs lost Matthew Boyd, Kevin Gausman, David Peterson, Clay Holmes, Shota Imanaga and Colin Rea to free agency, though all currently remain unsigned and any of them (Holmes is a great fit) could technically be brought back.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Marlins add SánchezThe Miami Marlins have agreed to terms with veteran catcher Gary Sánchez on a one-year, $6.5 million free-agent contract, ESPN reports. Sánchez, who soon turns 34, spent last season with the world-champion Milwaukee Brewers and served as William Contreras' productive backup. Long a power threat, Sánchez, for his career, has averaged 34 home runs per 162 games played to go with an OPS+ of 107. In Miami, he'll serve as Joe Mack's backup
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Bohm headed to RoyalsThe Royals and free agent corner infielder Alec Bohm have agreed to a two-year, $20 million deal, reports The Athletic. He's coming off a rough year in which he hit .249/.315/.383 (87 OPS+) with -0.2 WAR. He's gone as high as 20 home runs and 97 RBI in a season before, but he generally runs low-ish on-base percentages and scores negatively on defense. 
The Royals have an opening at third base after trading away Maikel Garcia earlier this offseason, so it seems like Bohm will get a chance to start alongside all-world shortstop Bobby Witt Jr.Arozarena, Suzuki down to three suitors?The top two free agent outfielders might be down to three suitors between the two of them. The Blue Jays, Phillies and Padres are in on Randy Arozarena and Seiya Suzuki, according to MLB Network.There are obvious fits with either player on any of the three teams. Arozarena, 31, is coming off his best all-around MLB season with 5.7 WAR. He hit .281/.381/.484 (148 OPS+) with 34 doubles, 26 home runs, 79 RBI, 26 steals and 113 runs. 
Suzuki, 32, greatly improved his defense in 2026, leading to a career-high WAR of 5.1. He hit .270/.368/.473 (131 OPS+) with 26 homers and 86 RBI. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mariners looking at relieversThe Mariners have had meetings with four free agent relief pitchers, per the Seattle Times. Three of them are left-handers Alex Vesia and Gregory Soto and right-hander Bryan Abreu.Abreu has been in the AL West for his whole career, having spent the entirety of his eight-year MLB career with the Astros. Last season, he had a 3.73 ERA and 80 strikeouts in 62 ⅔ innings, but walks have become a major issue. He issued 41 free passes. He's mostly been a primary setup man. 
Vesia had a 2.64 ERA and 1.07 WHIP with 74 strikeouts in 58 innings for the Dodgers last season. Soto posted a 3.63 ERA, 1.16 WHIP and 79 strikeouts in 67 innings. He has closing experience but has held several late-inning roles in his career. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Brewers bring back relieverThe Brewers have re-signed right-handed relief pitcher Antonio Senzatela on a one-year deal worth a reported $4.75 million, the ballclub announced Wednesday.
Senzatela was long a starting pitcher for the Rockies, but converted to relief and was traded to the Brewers in front of the deadline last season. In 57 appearances in the regular season, he worked 73 ⅓ innings with a 4.05 ERA and 1.35 WHIP. He proved valuable in the playoffs, going 4 ⅓ scoreless innings. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    D-backs starting pitchers available? Make sure not to misinterpret this report as the Diamondbacks actively shopping these guys, but "teams are checking on" D-backs starters Eduardo Rodríguez and Merrill Kelly, per The Athletic.Kelly, 38, was 10-14 with a 4.94 ERA in 162 innings last season and has one year and $20 million left on his deal. Any inquiring team would be hoping for a bounceback season, as Kelly had a 3.47 ERA in his previous four seasons. 
The 33-year-old Rodríguez might be a sell-high candidate here. There's one year and $19 million left on his contract and he's coming off his best season in a long time. He went 16-7 with a 2.89 ERA in 189 ⅔ innings. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    White Sox add outfielderFree agent outfielder Tyrone Taylor has signed with the White Sox on a two-year, $17 million contract, according to MLB.com.Taylor spent the last few months of last season in the same city with the Cubs and was excellent. In his 30 games on the North Side, he hit .351/.390/.500, spending time in all three outfield spots. Overall, he played in 97 games between the Mets and Cubs, posting 1.7 WAR as a fourth outfielder. 
Taylor now joins Sam Antonacci, Braden Montgomery, Andrew Benintendi, Brenton Doyle and Tristan Peters in the White Sox outfield mix.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mets looking for bench batAs the Mets continue to look for more pitching after the signing of Tarik Skubal, they are also "open to adding another outfielder as a bench bat," The Athletic reports.The Mets' current outfield is Juan Soto, A.J. Ewing and Carson Benge, with Nick Morabito as the bench option, though the latter may be ticketed for Triple-A to start the season should the Mets have their way. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Red Sox seek back-end rotation helpThe current Red Sox rotation is Garrett Crochet, Payton Tolle, Ranger Suárez, Jake Bennett and Brayan Bello. It's a quality fivesome, assuming everyone stays healthy. Therein lies the rub, of course, and you can never have too many starting pitchers. Sure enough, The Athletic reports that the Red Sox are seeking back-end rotation help. Among the listed options are Matthew Boyd, Robbie Ray and Hiromi Itoh, and any of those three would greatly bolster an already strong group.

Arsenal are still up there after falling just short in the 2026 final, while key injuries dent PSG's three-peat bid and Jose Mourinho has Real Madrid surging

        The Champions League season is still in the league phase, but we can start to look ahead into the new year with some teams performing better than others. Real Madrid, PSG and Arsenal are in great form, but there are also other teams that might improve in the second part of the season, when things will become more serious and everything will be decided. Let's go around Europe to see which are the best teams in the tournament right now. Here are the 10 teams capable of winning it all, ranked.10. AS RomaCan you imagine AS Roma challenging for the trophy? Well, it's very difficult, if not impossible, but this seems like a dreamy season for the Giallorossi so far, and their striker Donyell Malen is in stunning form. Gian Piero Gasperini was able to completely shape his team in his second season at the club. What a journey.9. Manchester CityThe Citizens are playing a season without knowing what will come next. The potential verdict coming in the near future and the fact they also replaced a manager like Pep Guardiola at the beginning of this campaign can definitely have an impact on their current performances and I don't see them potentially going for the title. For sure, they have the potential to bounce back and regain some confidence, considering the players they have available.8. InterThe Italian team didn't have their best start of the season but they are one of those sides that can drastically improve in the second half of the campaign, if they learn how to defend again. Inter played in two of the last four Champions League finals and have some experienced players who can help them to achieve that target again. It won't be easy, but they are one of those candidates that we need to keep in our minds in the second part of the season.
7. Atletico MadridNever underestimate a team coached by Diego Simeone. They are behind right now and unlikely to be a challenger for the trophy at the end of the season but we should always consider Atletico Madrid in the conversation. To make that happen, some things must change in the winter transfer window to improve their current squad. Not impossible, but also not very likely at this stage.6. LiverpoolSpeaking of teams that need to improve to reach the level of the top four at least, Liverpool is one of them. They replaced their coach in the summer and there are still too many ups and downs so far. Andoni Iraola is a coach with the experience and the capabilities to reach the later stages of the tournament, but it's difficult to imagine they can challenge the other big teams, at least based on what they have shown so far.5. Bayern MunichI would rate the German giants in a much higher position but we also need to understand they currently have their two best players, at least on paper, injured or not at their best. Harry Kane will miss at least three months of action while the future of Jamal Musiala is still uncertain due to his physical conditions. The big question is when and how this duo will be back, but Bayern can definitely be a challenger for the trophy.
4. BarcelonaThe Blaugrana are always part of this conversation, especially considering Lamine Yamal's ambitions to win the trophy and potentially win the next edition of the Ballon d'Or. Hansi Flick's target is to replicate his domestic success of the last two years in Europe.3. Real MadridJose Mourinho is back in action and Real Madrid are in great form, but more than anything, so are his players. Both Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham are probably playing their best season so far since they joined the Spanish giants, while Vinicius Jr is also hoping to reach his top form in the shortest time possible. They look particularly solid this season.2. PSGI would still consider them the leading candidates to win the tournament again, particularly after lifting the trophy in the past two editions, beating Inter and Arsenal in the respective finals. However, their chances have been significantly dented by injuries. Both Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are expected to miss the remainder of the season and, even if the club brings in replacements during the winter transfer window, losing two players of such importance is likely to have a major impact on their chances of retaining the title.
1. ArsenalThis has to be their season. Having finally won the Premier League last year, they now need to build on that success and consolidate their status at home, while also making a serious push for European glory. After coming so close last season, only to lose the 2026 final against PSG, they have every reason to believe they can go all the way.

title: Rams vs. Packers prediction: Can Green Bay continue success with deep ball? Will L.A. overcome injuries? - CBS Sports

body:
Micah Parsons makes his season debut for Green Bay as an injury-depleted Los Angeles offense leans on its ground attack in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve showdown
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:41 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve NFL game, the Los Angeles Rams play host to the Green Bay Packers. The Rams enter this game coming off their bye week, and they are incredibly banged up on offense. Puka Nacua is likely out for the year, as is Terrance Ferguson, after they each underwent surgery on lower-body injuries. Davante Adams remains out with his hamstring injury as well. The Rams will need their defense and their running backs to carry the day against a tough Packers team.Green Bay is also coming off the bye, but is getting healthier for this game as Micah Parsons will make his season debut after tearing his ACL toward the tail end of last season. Parsons returning to the fold provides a significant boost to what has already been a good defense under Jonathan Gannon, and the offense remains one of the league's most explosive units with Jordan Love targeting Christian Watson and Matthew Golden down the field.Will the Rams hold off the Packers at home, or will Green Bay pull off the upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.Where to watch Rams vs. Packers liveDate: Wednesday, Nov. 25 | Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: SoFi Stadium (Inglewood, California)Streaming: NetflixFollow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Rams -2.5, O/U 43.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Packers have the ballGreen Bay's offense is entirely based on the passing game because the Packers simply cannot run the ball. Green Bay is last in the league at 3.1 yards per carry. The Packers' 670 rushing yards are 124 fewer than the next-closest team in the league (the Bengals). The Rams allow only 3.9 yards per carry and sport Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald up front. 
The Packers are not going to find success on the ground here — and honestly, they might not even try to do so. They're probably just going to let Jordan Love drop back and let it rip. That's what they've largely done throughout this season, and it's worked quite well for them. Love has completed 63% of his passes at 7.7 yards per attempt, with 20 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He's ninth in the league in EPA per play, according to Tru Media, thanks largely to the fact that he's created explosives at the fourth-highest rate in the league. When you have Christian Watson and Matthew Golden by your side, that's how the offense is likely going to be built. The Packers really lean into their strengths by having the strong-armed Love target their speedy wideouts with deep routes; Love has thrown 20-plus yards downfield at the second-highest rate in football. The Rams have been the NFL's third-best defense against deep passes this year, according to Tru Media, with opponents completing only 8 of 30 deep passes for 257 yards, 1 touchdown and 1 interception. The 30 deep passes they've faced are the sixth-fewest in the league. 
It'll be fascinating to see whether Green Bay continues to attack deep downfield or if Love, Watson, Golden and tight end Tucker Kraft instead work the short and intermediate areas of the field that the Rams encourage opposing offenses to throw to because of their coverage structures. It'll also be interesting to see if Trent McDuffie shadows one of the two wideouts or if the Rams play sides with him and Josh Wallace, who has taken the place of the injured Jaylen Watson.L.A. has allowed the league's fewest catches and second-fewest yards to wide receivers this season, according to Pro-Football-Reference, with opposing quarterbacks targeting tight ends and running backs more often than they do against other teams. Tight ends have been targeted at the fourth-highest rate (27.4% of passes, according to Tru Media) against the Rams, while backs have been targeted at the second-highest rate (20.6%). This could be a game where Kraft is more involved in the proceedings. The Packers don't throw to their backs very often because they are not good players, so they'll probably still force the ball to Watson and Golden, even if the Rams do limit wide-receiver production.
When the Rams have the ballIn their first game without all three of Nacua, Adams and Ferguson, the Rams used a highly unusual personnel rotation. Their three leading skill-position players in snaps were all tight ends — and none of those tight ends was the one the Rams drafted in the second round. Their running backs shared the field for 18 snaps after having never previously played together in their careers, according to Tru Media. And one of their two primary wide receivers (rookie sixth-round pick CJ Daniels) played more than seven times as many snaps in Week 10 (44) as he had in his entire career before that (six).PlayerPositionSnapsColby ParkinsonTE52Davis AllenTE51Tyler HigbeeTE50Konata MumpfieldWR47CJ DanielsWR44Kyren WilliamsRB38Blake CorumRB37Ronnie RiversRB17Tutu AtwellWR15Xavier SmithWR9Max KlareTE4Brennan PresleyWR2The Rams were nevertheless able to rack up 436 yards, 28 first downs and 34 points against the decrepit Cardinals' defense. They ran the ball extremely well (202 yards) and were efficient in the passing game, with each of the wideouts creating an explosive play and the backs and tight ends chipping in with short and intermediate grabs. Matthew Stafford threw only 26 passes, but five of them created gains of at least 19 yards, and he averaged nearly 10 yards per attempt.
The Packers, though, are not the Cardinals. Green Bay enters this game allowing the third-fewest net yards per attempt in the league, which accounts for yardage lost due to sacks in addition to passing yards allowed. The Packers have also yielded only 15 touchdowns through the air while intercepting a league-high 14 passes. Their safeties, in particular, have been ballhawks, with Evan Williams and Xavier McKinney combining for nine of those 14 picks and McKinney leading the league with six on his own.Green Bay has been just about average in generating pressure so far this season, recording a sack, hit or hurry on 36.2% of opponent dropbacks, according to Tru Media. (The league average is 36.4% this year.) Getting Parsons back in the fold should help tremendously. He led the NFL in total pressures between 2021 and 2025 despite rushing the passer considerably less often than players like Myles Garrett and Maxx Crosby, who are the only players within 30 pressures of Parsons' total during that span. Parsons will likely play limited snaps, but those snaps should be concentrated on important downs and Matthew Stafford and Co. will need to be aware of where he is at all times.The Packers have also done a pretty strong job of limiting opposing run games, allowing only 4.0 yards per carry. The Rams, though, have sported one of the best rushing attacks in the league, with Williams and Corum combining to average 4.6 yards a pop. The offensive line has cleared the way for 1.79 yards before contact per attempt, which is the second-best mark in the league behind only that of the Bills. Williams and Corum (and Ronnie Rivers) also have a combined 21.0% avoided tackle rate, per Tru Media, which is the seventh-best in football.
The Rams will likely have to lean on their run game here to move the ball, because the situation does not line up well for them through the air. The offensive line's ability to dictate the game at the line of scrimmage will likely determine whether they can achieve any degree of offensive success.PredictionThe lift the Packers get from Micah Parsons' return, plus the limitations the Rams' offense should have while working without Nacua, Adams and Ferguson, push me toward Green Bay in this game. I don't foresee the Rams moving the ball as consistently against the Packers as they did against the Cardinals in their first game without all their playmakers. Meanwhile, the Packers have the goods to challenge L.A.'s secondary downfield with Watson and Golden and over the middle with Kraft. Love should be able to get going through the air, even if Green Bay still can't run the ball. Pick: Packers 24, Rams 17

This is the time of year when all the preseason optimism can go away in a hurry. Beating up on lesser competition in non-conference play is all fun and games. This is the meat and potatoes where the big dawgs go toe-to-toe. Strengths and weaknesses will be on full display.

Duke can do that too, with big man Patrick Ngongba holding down the fort on the back end. He has to avoid foul trouble, but Duke has the size, strength and length on the perimeter with Caleb Foster, Dame Sarr and Sebastian Wilkins to give some of UConn's shooters some issues.  


Turning defense into offense has to be the recipe for Duke because I don't think this offense is in a great position right now to score against a set UConn halfcourt defense. Silas Demary Jr. and Jayden Ross are just way too good defensively, and Duke hasn't found the right mix offensively. That said, Duke is due to make some shots, and it's the deeper, bigger team. body:
Steelers players spoke favorably about Aaron Rodgers after his release, while team sources reportedly corroborated portions of the quarterback's explosive criticism of Mike McCarthy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        While Aaron Rodgers was publicly scorching Mike McCarthy, several Steelers watched their now-former teammate inside the locker room following Wednesday's practice. It was a surreal moment in a truly bizarre 24 hours for the Steelers, who ultimately released Rodgers after his criticism of McCarthy. Pittsburgh announced late Tuesday night that Rodgers would be inactive against the Broncos and would be replaced by Mason Rudolph. Rodgers, during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, accused McCarthy of being late and sleeping through meetings, not watching film of opponents the week of games and saying, "1-2-3 Packers!" in the locker room at halftime during Sunday's eventual loss to the Eagles. McCarthy has since confirmed his Packers snafu in a press conference, calling it an embarrassing moment.Anonymous team sources corroborated Rodgers' claim that McCarthy fell asleep in meetings, according to The Athletic."He's not lying," an unnamed player said. Several players were interviewed at their locker, including tight end Pat Freiermuth, rookie quarterback Drew Allar, rookie receiver Germie Bernard, and veteran wideout Marquez Valdes-Scantling, who was also Rodgers' teammate in Green Bay. Each spoke favorably about Rodgers. 
"I think he's the best player to ever play this game as his position," Valdes-Scantling said. 
Rodgers said that Freiermuth informed him Tuesday night of the Steelers' decision to deactivate him. "I was just checking in on a close friend," Freiermuth said. 
Allar started to address questions about Rodgers but stopped after he was waived off by veteran safety DeShon Elliott. 
"For me, it's kinda sad to see, because I have a lot of respect for Aaron," Allar said. "I've learned a lot from him since he's been here. I think I'm gonna leave it at that and just with Aaron the best." 
Bernard shared a message that McCarthy told the team earlier in the day. "Just gotta come together. It's all about unity," he said. "Coach told us today that the best teams are player-led, and we have all the veterans, we have all the talent in the world to do that. So we just have to lean on each other." Bernard also exuded confidence in Rudolph, who will make his first start of the season Friday against the Broncos. 
"Mason is a great quarterback," he said. "We have complete trust in him, and he has complete trust in us. We've just got to go out there and believe in what he can do so we can get it done."

title: Steelers release Aaron Rodgers following criticism of Mike McCarthy: Possible landing spots for QB - CBS Sports
description: Rodgers will get a chance to finish his career elsewhere if he chooses
body:
Rodgers will get a chance to finish his career elsewhere if he chooses
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Aaron Rodgers' time with the Pittsburgh Steelers has ended after he heavily criticized Mike McCarthy hours after Pittsburgh made him inactive for Friday's game against the Broncos. Shortly after his criticism, the Steelers announced that they had released the quarterback, and he officially hit the waiver wire Wednesday afternoon. Any team can sign Rodgers until 4 p.m. ET on Thursday. If no team claims him by then, he will become a free agent. Rodgers, 42, had re-signed with the Steelers in hopes of finishing his career with a successful reunion with McCarthy, his coach with the Packers from 2006-18. Instead, Rodgers will look to finish his career elsewhere. It appears that Rodgers' breakup with Pittsburgh was the result of a disagreement between Rodgers and McCarthy over play-calling duties. The Steelers had been running more hurry-up offense in recent weeks. In that situation, the play-calling duties are more split between Rodgers and quarterbacks coach Tom Arth. McCarthy clearly wanted a more collaborative approach. 
Rodgers said that his desire to handle more of the play-calling duties was a byproduct of, in his words, McCarthy being late and sleeping through team meetings. Rodgers said that McCarthy said, "1-2-3, Packers!" at halftime during Pittsburgh's Week 11 loss to the Eagles. Rodgers said that was essentially the last straw and decided to address his concerns with McCarthy this week. Those discussions led to the end of Rodgers' time with the Steelers, who will face the Broncos on Friday with Mason Rudolph under center. While the Steelers move ahead, Rodgers will now try to figure out his next move. Here are five possible landing spots for Rodgers, who did not say whether he still plans to retire after this season, given what has transpired over the last 24 hours. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    New England Patriots At this point, there are only two realistic possibilities for Rodgers if he wants to be a starter. The best option of the two is New England, who recently lost Drake Maye to a potentially season-ending injury. The Patriots have lost three out of their last four games, but they still have a decent shot at making the playoffs, especially if the Steelers fall off without Rodgers. New England has a chance to get back over .500 this week if they can defeat the 1-9 Chargers in Los Angeles. Would Rodgers make much of a difference? He would be an upgrade over Tommy DeVito, but the odds of the Patriots actually defending their AFC title are slim either way. The Patriots have struggled on both sides of the ball this year and have four games left against teams with winning records. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Baltimore RavensBaltimore is in a total freefall. After a 2-0 start, the Ravens have lost seven straight games and are sitting by themselves in the AFC North cellar. Lamar Jackson's season-ending injury essentially ended Baltimore's season. The Ravens recently acquired Jacoby Brissett, who played relatively well in close losses to the Chargers and Texans. There's a chance, however, that the Ravens may decide to add Rodgers to their quarterback room to see if he can provide a further spark. Baltimore would also gain an advantage from an intel standpoint if they signed Rodgers. The Ravens have two upcoming games against Pittsburgh, their longtime rival. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    San Francisco 49ersThis is mostly a nostalgia move. Rodgers is a California native who grew up a diehard 49ers fan. The 49ers famously passed on him in the 2005 NFL Draft, and Rodgers has never been shy about his desire to show his childhood team they made a big mistake. In this scenario, Rodgers would have the chance to go home and play for his childhood team, albeit in a backup role. He also could serve as a mentor for Brock Purdy, who is having an MVP-caliber season. Given the 49ers' injury history, Kyle Shanahan probably wouldn't mind having a backup with Rodgers' experience. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Green Bay Packers Another nostalgia move that would be largely ceremonial. While his exit from Green Bay wasn't perfect, Rodgers is currently on good terms with both Matt LaFleur and Jordan Love. Unlike his mentor, Brett Favre, Rodgers could close out his career with the team that shaped his NFL legacy. 
It wouldn't be the perfect ending, but a return to Green Bay — even as a backup — would give Rodgers some semblance of closure to what has been a Hall of Fame career. Retirement Rodgers can also retire, which may or may not come on his terms. If he goes unclaimed and no one signs him this season, Rodgers would have to wait to see if another team comes calling this offseason, which might not happen. It's very possible that Rodgers wouldn't have played this season if the Steelers didn't offer him a chance to return. Rodgers wouldn't be the first professional athlete to retire that way. In fact, there are a host of great players across numerous sports who have had their careers end in a similar fashion, albeit without the scorched-earth interview. Players seldom get the John Elway retirement where they get to ride off into the sunset with a championship. More often than not, players are told when the ride is over. That can happen to Rodgers, or he can choose to shape the narrative by calling it quits on his own terms.

body:
A 2-2 draw with Roma revealed an attack missing its usual bite, raising questions about whether long-term knee injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue have stripped the European champions of their fear factor
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 25, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Have Paris Saint-Germain been defanged? It is too soon to say if injuries have laid low the Champions League's biggest beast, but on the evidence of Wednesday's 2-2 draw with Roma, there might not be quite the same fear factor when opponents find themselves face to face with the kings of Europe's jungle.Without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, both of whom are expected to miss most, if not all, of this season with knee injuries, there simply was not the final-third threat in PSG's ranks to keep Roma honest without the ball. That was all the more pronounced given that Ousmane Dembele was left on the bench until the penalty with which PSG took a 2-1 lead. Maghnes Akliouche, Senny Mayulu and Ferran Torres are talented forwards, the last good enough to win a World Cup final for Spain. Pair one or even two of them with the potential Ballon d'Or winners who started for PSG in the Champions League final, and the drop-off is not particularly significant.Of course, it might be that Luis Enrique is not particularly minded to see how good his reserves could be flanking Dembele. It would make sense. The Frenchman's fitness needs careful managing at the best of times. With PSG having won their first four league-phase games, there was no pressing need to load up minutes on a player who will surely be needed in the spring. It was a similar story at the base of PSG's team, Ilia Zabarnyi preferred to Marquinhos, another who does well to hit a dozen games before Christmas. This might be a vision of the months ahead for an injury-addled PSG, but it might just be a team that has never taken the league phase particularly seriously not taking the league phase particularly seriously.Whatever the longer-term view, on the field this evening, PSG's attack lacked the bite to keep Roma backing off. There is a good chance that any team managed by Gian Piero Gasperini might just go man-to-man whoever the opposition, but the fearlessness with which the Giallorossi hurtled around the Parc des Princes was a sure sign they weren't checking over their shoulder quite as much.Instead, they felt empowered to push on, center back Mario Hermoso on hand to roll in the opener inside the box after an excellent run by Matias Soule. Again, the caveat to assessing how future opponents might take on PSG is that Hermoso has been box-crashing from defense all through this season. You can't be sure he wouldn't have been in the same spot even if he were marking Doue or Kvaratskhelia.
What you can know is that Roma's aggression when PSG had the ball in open play was not what cost them. Nuno Mendes' ability to blow by his man created issues, and Achraf Hakimi got his usual shots and shot assists from advanced positions. They could have beaten Roma, but aside from the fullbacks and a few darts into the area by Joao Neves, there was not much to scare Mile Svilar in the champions' lineup.Instead, it was familiar failings that cost Roma, who might be a real dark horse for this competition when they can successfully defend a corner. Zabarnyi did not even have to win a duel to turn Mayulu's delivery home, just standing in the space between two white shirts at the near post. PSG's second, from the penalty spot, was a Roma confection too. Wesley could argue that Svilar should have been off his line quicker when Hakimi charged in behind, but did the Brazilian need to put his arms on his man at the exact moment he broke into the box? Wesley was lucky not to get a straight red.In such favorable positions, prime PSG often blitz their opponents. This time, even with Dembele on the field, they could not get clear. Gasperini had an ace of his own on the bench, Donyell Malen sparking Roma after his introduction. A driving run and cutback from the left had PSG scrambling, Vitinha's arm blocking a shot to hand the visitors a penalty that Malen converted.
Had a third goal come, it would probably have been for Roma, Hermoso blazing over late on. There was something more in this for Roma, who remain outside the top 24 despite such impressive displays against Real Madrid, Manchester United and now the holders. As for PSG, there will be time for Luis Enrique to work out how his side dominates Europe with its attack so limited. It would appear there is work to do.
